text:
maya: Heads up — customer Parcelly (hosted) reporting intermittent 504s + timeouts for lot of generation calls over last 30m. Spike correlated with high concurrent chat traffic. gateway -> continuous-batching looks suspect.

support-ops: Ticket INC-4981 created and customer trace samples requested. They say requests hang ~28-32s then 504. :grimacing:

jon: Can you drop a sample trace id and a tiny log excerpt? Need gateway/request IDs to correlate with metrics.

maya: Sample trace id: trc_000abc123. Gateway log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T14:11:02Z gateway-12 WARN req=trc_000abc123 tenant=parcelly queue_wait=29000ms status=504
2026-03-17T14:11:03Z gateway-12 INFO req=trc_000abc124 tenant=parcelly routed=batcher-7 batch_id=bb-442 wait_ms=28000
```

srebot: ALERT continuous_batcher.backlog > 500 for region=us-west (rule: cb.backlog.threshold=300)

alex: Looking at Prometheus snapshot around the spike:
```
continuous_batcher.backlog{pod=batcher-7,tenant="parcelly"} 682
request_queue.depth{pod=gateway-12,tenant="parcelly"} 1745
kv_cache.spinups{pod=batcher-7} 102
kv_cache.miss_rate{tenant="parcelly"} 0.78
inference.seq_len.p95{tenant="parcelly"} 1024
```

lina: That kv_cache.spinups + high miss_rate + long seq_len smells like prefix-diversity thrash. If the KV cache keeps evicting, batchers can't reuse KV and requests stall while kv is built.

jon: Repro steps requested from support — can the customer share a minimal payload? Or we can try to replay recorded traffic to a staging pool.

maya: Customer provided a small repro that hits many unique conversation prefixes rapidly. They can allow a replay to our staging (consent confirmed).

eng-runtime: Immediate mitigation suggestions (temp, per-tenant):
- reduce continuous_batcher.max_batch_size from 16 -> 4
- lower continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms from 50 -> 20
- bump gateway.request_queue_depth for tenant from 500 -> 2000 (soft limit)
- enable fallback routing to redwood-mini-quant8 for parcelly to reduce per-token time/cold-kv cost
These should reduce batch assembly latency and KV churn.

jon: Command to apply per-tenant config (run from ops CLI):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.internal/tenants/parcelly/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"continuous_batcher": {"max_batch_size": 4, "max_wait_ms": 20}, "gateway": {"request_queue_depth": 2000}, "routing": {"fallback_model": "redwood-mini-quant8"}}'
```

deploy-bot: Applied tenant config to pool rp-42. change_id=chg_77f3a (user=jon) — success.

alex: Post-change snap (5m after):
```
continuous_batcher.backlog{tenant="parcelly"} 12
request_queue.depth{tenant="parcelly"} 210
inference.p95.latency{tenant="parcelly"} 1800ms -> was 12s
kv_cache.spinups{tenant="parcelly"} 6
```

support-ops: Customer confirmed immediate improvement: p95 reduced to ~1.8s, no 504s in last 10m. Customer on call is happy with the temporary fix. :thumbsup:

eng-runtime: Follow-ups for root cause/perm fix:
- add per-tenant kv_cache.pinlist or prefix-collapsing option
- improve batching heuristics to avoid building massive KV for tiny divergent prefixes
- add a soft-queue-limit alarm (notify SRE) before hard queue saturation
- evaluate default continuous_batcher defaults for high-diversity chat workloads

lina: I'll open a follow-up RFC and include replay traces + metrics and link to this thread.

maya: Filing incident doc and linking ticket INC-4981 -> internal incident runbook for postmortem. Next steps: plan kv cache improvements and tenant isolation for noisy prefixes.

support-ops: Closing immediate escalation. Will monitor for 24h and reopen if regressions.

jon: Thanks team — nice quick mitigation. Will coordinate timeline for permanent fixes with eng-runtime.
